text: This project's convention for anything between staging and marts is int underscore entity underscore underscore verb-ed. This model joins orders to customers, so it's int_orders__joined.

Two ref calls, not source — this model reads from other models, which is exactly what makes it intermediate. Ref to the customers mart from the Beginner project, ref to the orders staging model from Lesson 3, joined on customer_id.

Left join, specifically. Every order should have a matching customer, but left join keeps every order row even if a customer record is ever missing. An inner join here would make orders silently disappear from downstream totals, with no error raised at all.

Deliberately not here yet: payments, a revenue total, or incremental materialization. This model's only job is orders joined to who placed them. Payments join in starting Lesson 6 — and that's also where this chapter's real risk gets introduced on purpose.
Next lesson: why this model needs to be incremental — the daily-growing orders table finally forces the materialization choice this chapter has been building toward since Lesson 1.
